name: codewhale
description: First-party Codewhale extensions: the plugins and skills Codewhale ships, maintained in the open so anyone can propose a change.

plugins.name: computer-use
plugins.description: See the screen and operate it: accessibility-first control, screenshots and zoom on macOS, Windows and Linux, plus macOS recording and HarmonyOS devices over hdc.

plugins.name: batch
plugins.description: Break a large, parallelizable goal into bounded work units, coordinate existing agent/worktree machinery, integrate, and verify. Explicit-only.

plugins.name: best-of-n
plugins.description: Generate a small set of independent candidate solutions in worktrees, judge them against one explicit rubric, and apply the winner only after PASS verification.

plugins.name: contributor-onboarding
plugins.description: Help a new contributor get productive on this checkout - inspect sync state against main, build, run the repository's exact verification gate, and produce a local what's-new digest. Never fetches, pulls, or modifies a dirty tree on its own. Explicit-only.

plugins.name: dataviz
plugins.description: Choose and produce an appropriate chart/dashboard/visual explanation from data, with legible encodings and source/assumption notes.

plugins.name: debug
plugins.description: Reproduce, minimize, localize, identify root cause, and distinguish diagnosis from an authorized fix. Prefer root-cause over symptom patches.

plugins.name: delegate
plugins.description: Strategic delegation for multi-step coding, research, or verification work. Use when a task can be split into parent reasoning plus focused sub-agent execution through the agent tool.

plugins.name: dependency-update
plugins.description: Read release notes/changelogs, update a defined dependency scope, handle breaking changes, and verify. Explicit-only; no broad update-everything by inference.

plugins.name: document
plugins.description: Write or update repository/product documentation: README, user guides, API docs, architecture, migration notes, and changelog material. This is not the Word-document artifact skill.

plugins.name: documents
plugins.description: Compatibility alias for the docx skill. Prefer loading docx.

plugins.name: docx
plugins.description: Create/edit/inspect Word documents using available managed or host capabilities.

plugins.name: feishu
plugins.description: Work with Feishu or Lark bots, docs, sheets, bitables, approval flows, and OpenAPI/MCP setup without hardcoding credentials.

plugins.name: fleet-manager
plugins.description: Use when managing, triaging, restarting, escalating, or summarizing Codewhale fleet runs and workers.

plugins.name: frontend-design
plugins.description: Produce intentional, responsive, accessible UI work and perform visual QA instead of generic component assembly.

plugins.name: help
plugins.description: Route a "how do I use Codewhale" question to the installed help, config, and doctor surfaces instead of reciting a manual from memory. Explicit-only.

plugins.name: implement
plugins.description: Carry an authorized, defined request or approved plan through scoped edits and proportionate verification. Skill loading is not write authorization by itself.

plugins.name: interview
plugins.description: Ask one useful structured question at a time only when material product/implementation choices are genuinely missing; remember answers and produce a brief/spec. Discoverable facts should be investigated instead of asked.

plugins.name: mcp-builder
plugins.description: Design, build, configure, or debug Model Context Protocol servers for codewhale, including stdio and HTTP/SSE transports.

plugins.name: mcp-discovery
plugins.description: Find and start a zero-environment local MCP server when the session lacks a capability that no available tool, project script, or ordinary local code can cover.

plugins.name: pdf
plugins.description: Read, extract, split, merge, rotate, watermark, fill, OCR, or create PDF files with verification of page counts and text extraction.

plugins.name: plan
plugins.description: Turn a sufficiently understood task into an ordered implementation plan with dependencies and verification. Orchestrate Codewhale’s native plan state; do not build a parallel planner.

plugins.name: plugin-creator
plugins.description: Scaffold a local Codewhale plugin bundle with a versioned manifest, namespaced Skills, and an explicit trust review.

plugins.name: pptx
plugins.description: Create/edit/inspect/verify slide decks and PPTX presentations.

plugins.name: presentations
plugins.description: Compatibility alias for the pptx skill. Prefer loading pptx.

plugins.name: release
plugins.description: Prepare a named version: preflight, version consistency, build/package, smoke test, checksums/notes, and release readiness. Publishing/tagging/deploy need separate authorization. Explicit-only.

plugins.name: research
plugins.description: Current external research using available web tools, primary sources where possible, links/citations, date awareness, synthesis, and unresolved uncertainty.

plugins.name: review
plugins.description: Read-only correctness review with actionable findings first, tight file/line evidence, severity, and a concise residual-risk summary.

plugins.name: security-review
plugins.description: Review trust boundaries, auth/authz, injection, secrets, filesystem/network exposure, dependencies, and exploitability without pretending a shallow lint is an audit.

plugins.name: simplify
plugins.description: Improve clarity and reduce needless complexity after behavior is understood; preserve behavior and keep cleanup separate from correctness fixes.

plugins.name: skill-creator
plugins.description: Create or improve codewhale skills. Use when the user wants a new skill, wants to update an existing skill, or needs guidance on when a skill should be a skill versus MCP, hooks, tools, or a plugin scaffold.

plugins.name: skill-installer
plugins.description: Install, update, trust, or inspect Codewhale skills from GitHub or local skill folders. Use when the user asks for available skills or wants a community skill installed.

plugins.name: spreadsheets
plugins.description: Compatibility alias for the xlsx skill. Prefer loading xlsx.

plugins.name: test
plugins.description: Detect the project’s test stack, run the narrowest useful tests, create tests when authorized, and report coverage/gaps honestly.

plugins.name: v4-best-practices
plugins.description: Use when working with deepseek-v4-pro or deepseek-v4-flash in thinking mode on multi-step or plan-driven tasks. Provides rules to prevent stale references, unverified plan assumptions, and vague plan output.

plugins.name: verify
plugins.description: Exercise the real app/API/CLI and collect observable evidence; tests alone do not count as end-to-end verification.

plugins.name: webapp-testing
plugins.description: Start/reuse a local app, wait for readiness, inspect rendered state/console/network, act from observed selectors, and verify with evidence.

plugins.name: xlsx
plugins.description: Create/edit/analyze/verify spreadsheet workbooks including XLSX/CSV/TSV.
